Replay

Igniter tongues and spread bolts

3 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓
On this page ↓
Compatibility

The igniter now draws the original ASCII * tongues: five on the caster's predicted view at −0.5, −0.25, 0, 0.25 and 0.5 radians, one on remote observed views. Each starts 18 pixels from the origin, advances 10 pixels per displayed simulation tick and expires after 15 ticks. Those fixed visual constants match the original even when a custom cone's gameplay range differs. Labels are centered on their flight position. Forward observations sweep living observed mob circles to retire contacted tongues; the instantaneous cone's damage/status rule is unchanged. Original contact bursts/flashes and exact frame-time feel still need paired evaluation.

Spread reactions now record an explicit Flash.Arc before each target re-enters the status rulebook. It stores the actual source/destination, carried status and credit in the existing bounded flash pool. The renderer uses the original four- point kink with a seven-pixel displacement and two-pixel half-width, yielding an eight-vertex polygon. It uses the payload RGB, base alpha 0.8 and depth 8, with the original expansion/fade curve over the existing 17-tick flash lifetime. Zero-length hops are retained as facts but draw no bolt, matching the original renderer. All arcs use observed state, including on the causer's screen.

Flame/arc nodes are created on first use and reused within bounded pools. Hiding, slot replacement, rewinds and epoch changes reset the relevant view state. Arc positions are recorded facts, so later target motion or deletion cannot redirect a bolt to a new occupant. Correction/removal/expiry controls visibility; recovery continues the saved lifetime rather than replaying an old launch.

Compatibility#

Arc paths introduced content 0x5253435241503046; dash actions subsequently introduced 0x5253435241503047. Adding the Arc enum member changed the canonical schema/contract while the World remained 52,600 bytes. Gameplay protocol 7 and checkpoint layout 4 were unchanged by that transition. Older peers fail admission; older saves require the explicit offline converter. The save guide records the current content identity and accepted input formats.

The converter paths for contents 42–45 use frozen old World/Flash and event/action descriptors, map World fields and pending actions, and retain the existing identity, outcomes, inputs and asset checks. The content-45 fixture was created with the actual old converter before the enum changed. Existing destinations and source files are never overwritten. Earlier shared value types remain reused where their shape is unchanged; future changes must preserve those source shapes.

Shell
nix develop --command bash examples/replay_scrapyard/cast_path_run.sh
REPLAY_PREBUILT=1 RSY_HEADED_HOST=1 RSY_AUDIO_DRIVER=Dummy \
  RSY_PATH_CAPTURE=/absolute/existing/output/directory \
  GODOT=/path/to/Godot bash examples/replay_scrapyard/cast_path_run.sh

The native scene chooses its loadout during staging, casts the cone, then primes and shocks a player beside two static barrels through existing development actions. It checks the fan, centered glyph flight, two actual target bolts and expiry. Browser acceptance checks five local versus one remote tongue, then recorded hops to two barrels and the two other players. Model tests cover exact geometry, actual hop payload/credit, bounded dense spread and checkpoint restoration/expiry.

Remaining launch/contact feedback, broader platform coverage, audio listening and paired feel/authoring/runtime comparisons remain requirements. See evidence and the port ledger.

The renderer now uses immutable ArrayMesh instances for procedural polygons. Color/alpha use instance self modulation; arcs reuse one unit polygon and an affine basis that preserves the existing kink, width and recorded endpoints. Node pools, visibility, lifetimes and simulation formats remain unchanged. This avoids the stock web renderer's Polygon2D index-update path, including during viewport resize. See the rendering audit.
